title: “The beginning of knowledge” — the Greek has “the beginning of wisdom”
summary: The KJV of Proverbs 1:7 says the fear of the Lord is “the beginning of knowledge” and that fools despise “wisdom and instruction”. Brenton’s Greek prints a word that Brenton’s English renders “wisdom” at the first place, and then adds two clauses about understanding and piety.
text: KJV Proverbs 1:7: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.” Hebrew (WLC) 1:7: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה רֵאשִׁ֣ית דָּ֑עַת. Brenton’s Greek 1:7: Ἀρχὴ σοφίας φόβος. Brenton’s own English (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/PRO01.htm) prints: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; and there is good understanding to all that practise it: and piety toward God is the beginning of discernment”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/1/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO01.htm.
reasoning: Both texts say the fear of the Lord is a beginning. The KJV names what it begins as “knowledge” and uses “wisdom” in the second clause for what fools despise. The Greek names it with σοφίας, which Brenton’s English renders “wisdom”, and then adds two clauses the KJV verse does not have: one about good understanding for those who practise it, and one that calls piety toward God “the beginning of discernment”. So the KJV and the Greek name different things as what the fear of the Lord begins, and the Greek is longer.

title: “Train up a child in the way he should go” — Brenton’s Greek prints no verse 22:6
summary: The KJV of Proverbs 22:6 reads “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” Brenton’s Greek of chapter 22 prints verse 5 and then verse 7, and a search of Brenton’s English of the whole book finds no verse that says this.
text: KJV Proverbs 22:5–7: “Thorns and snares are in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.” “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” “The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.” Hebrew (WLC) 22:6: חֲנֹ֣ךְ לַ֭נַּעַר עַל־פִּ֣י דַרְכֹּ֑ו גַּ֥ם כִּֽי־יַ֝זְקִ֗ין לֹֽא־יָס֥וּר מִמֶּֽנָּה. Brenton’s Greek 22:5: Τρίβολοι καὶ παγίδες ἐν ὁδοῖς σκολιαῖς. Brenton’s Greek 22:7: Πλούσιοι πτωχῶν ἄρξουσι. The page prints no verse numbered 22:6. title: “The words of a talebearer are as wounds” — the Greek of 18:8 has “Fear casts down the slothful”
summary: The KJV of Proverbs 18:8 says “The words of a talebearer are as wounds”. Brenton’s Greek of 18:8 says “Fear casts down the slothful; and the souls of the effeminate shall hunger”. The Hebrew of 26:22 repeats the words of 18:8, and Brenton’s Greek of 26:22 is worded differently from its 18:8.
text: KJV Proverbs 18:8: “The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.” Hebrew (WLC) 18:8: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן. Brenton’s Greek 18:8: Ὀκνηροὺς καταβάλλει φόβος. Brenton’s own English (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/PRO18.htm) prints: “Fear casts down the slothful; and the souls of the effeminate shall hunger”. KJV Proverbs 26:22: “The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.” Hebrew (WLC) 26:22: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן. Brenton’s own English (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/PRO26.htm) prints at 26:22: “The words of cunning knaves are soft”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/18/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/20/26/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PRO18.htm.
reasoning: The KJV’s 18:8 has a subject, the talebearer’s words, and a comparison with wounds. The Greek of 18:8 has no talebearer and no wounds: it names fear as what casts down the slothful and says what happens to the souls of the effeminate. The finding is the difference at 18:8.

title: “A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit” — the Greek has “He that becomes surety for a man charged with murder shall be an exile”
summary: The KJV of Proverbs 28:17 says the man who does violence to a person’s blood shall flee to the pit. Brenton’s Greek says the one who becomes surety for a man charged with murder shall be an exile.
